summary: Iteration 37 (mobile 390×844) frontend-only verification: iOS zoom-prevention + rating popup restructure + accounting KPI/expense-row mobile layout. ALL 7 review items PASS on 390×844 viewport.
critical_code_review_comments: React hydration warning in console: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Some <select><option>{...}</option></select> block is wrapping a <span> inside <option>, which is invalid HTML. Not blocking any current flow but worth cleaning up. Grep for `<option` and check for nested spans in AccountingPage / another select. Non-critical.

AccountingPage.jsx is 1278 lines and hosts 6 subtabs + 3 sub-components. Recommend splitting each subtab (Overview/Monthly/Invoices/Expenses/Accounts/Income) into its own file for maintainability. Not blocking.

RatingPopup.jsx forces `style={{ fontSize: '16px' }}` on the textarea AND has a global CSS `input:not(...)` rule that already sets 16px on ≤640px. The double-fix is defensive/good, but note the inline style now applies on DESKTOP too — desktop keeps 16px on this textarea whereas other CSS-rule inputs get their native (smaller) desktop size. Non-blocking cosmetic.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 test expense (TEST_ITER37 Beleg, CHF 89.50) since the Ausgaben list was empty, in order to inspect a real expense-row mobile layout. Attempted immediate cleanup via delete button + confirm dialog handler after inspection.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 37 = pure CSS/layout change. Baseline (Iter 34/36) still holds; backend not re-tested this iteration. Rating-cell selector in the app is `fk-cell-{sub_id}-{lesson_id}` (NOT `rating-cell-...` as the review request claimed). Student list items use `admin-student-open-{id}` and `admin-student-row-{id}`. The global CSS rule `@media (max-width: 640px) input:not([type='checkbox']):not([type='radio']):not([type='range']), select, textarea { font-size: 16px !important; }` correctly hits ALL relevant inputs on 390px viewport including native date pickers, number inputs, selects. If future auth-related inputs (e.g., login) need testing on mobile, they already inherit the 16px rule.
